commit.message:
[dawn] Minor fix for sizeof on bitfield

Looks like when dawn assert are disabled we fall down into a
macro for DAWN_ASSERT that uses sizeof(conditional).

This for logical reasons is not allowed.

I could find an easy fix to Assert.h so lets fix this for now
this way.

commit.subject: Remove WaitForSingleObject call in SynchronizeBufferBeforeMapping
commit.message:
Remove WaitForSingleObject call in SynchronizeBufferBeforeMapping

ID3D12Fence::SetEventOnCompletion will synchronously wait for the
fence to reach the passed in signal value if you pass a null HANDLE.

Calling WaitForSingleObject on null HANDLE, on the other hand,
will return an error and set the last error into an error state.

This CL removes the WaitForSingleObject call and passes a null HANDLE
to SetEventOnCompletion.

Bug: chromium:407748576
Change-Id: I104f432c4397757a5b48f9c2f62762c4a5162315

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Add part of the validation of dynamic array mutators.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Add part of the validation of dynamic array mutators.

All the validation that's synchronous and doesn't look at which binding
is potentially used on the GPU, as well as the validation that generates
validation errors.

 - Adds a wgpu::Status to RemoveBinding to report error.
 - Adds wgpu::kInvalidBinding to report InsertBindingErrors.
 - Support dynamic array in BindGroupBase::MakeError. This is required
   because we need to do "content timeline" state tracking even on error
   bindgroups, but only the ones that had a dynamic binding array
   specified.
 - Factor out ValidateDynamicBindingArrayEntry that's now used both in
   bindgroup creation and Update().
 - Allow destroying error bindgroups that have a dynamic array. This is
   allowed in the bindless proposal because the content-timeline doesn't
   know if a bindgroup is an error or not.
 - Add tests for all the synchronous validation, updated validation
   rules and some of the validation generating validations errors.

Bug: 462600012, 435317394
Change-Id: I3daba64a77db5ec82397c5cc6b161e6725f0dae6

[dawn][native] Add part of the validation of dynamic array mutators.

All the validation that's synchronous and doesn't look at which binding
is potentially used on the GPU, as well as the validation that generates
validation errors.

 - ASSERT in BindGroupLayoutBase::IsEmpty that we have an internal
   layout (this is called only on valid BGLs).
 - Adds a wgpu::Status to RemoveBinding to report error.
 - Adds wgpu::kInvalidBinding to report InsertBindingErrors.
 - Support dynamic array in BindGroupBase::MakeError. This is required
   because we need to do "content timeline" state tracking even on error
   bindgroups, but only the ones that had a dynamic binding array
   specified.
 - Factor out ValidateDynamicBindingArrayEntry that's now used both in
   bindgroup creation and Update().
 - Allow destroying error bindgroups that have a dynamic array. This is
   allowed in the bindless proposal because the content-timeline doesn't
   know if a bindgroup is an error or not.
 - Add tests for all the synchronous validation, updated validation
   rules and some of the validation generating validations errors.

Bugs found with testing:

 - Inversion of the condition for OOB checks on slots.
 - Missing validation of OOB check for the start of the dynamic array.
 - Missed check for frontend layout validity before trying to get the
   BindGroupLayoutInternal.
 - Missing validation of a destroyed dynamic binding array in
   RemoveBinding.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Add part of the validation of dynamic array mutators.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Add part of the validation of dynamic array mutators.

All the validation that's synchronous and doesn't look at which binding
is potentially used on the GPU, as well as the validation that generates
validation errors.

 - ASSERT in BindGroupLayoutBase::IsEmpty that we have an internal
   layout (this is called only on valid BGLs).
 - Adds a wgpu::Status to RemoveBinding to report error.
 - Adds wgpu::kInvalidBinding to report InsertBindingErrors.
 - Support dynamic array in BindGroupBase::MakeError. This is required
   because we need to do "content timeline" state tracking even on error
   bindgroups, but only the ones that had a dynamic binding array
   specified.
 - Factor out ValidateDynamicBindingArrayEntry that's now used both in
   bindgroup creation and Update().
 - Allow destroying error bindgroups that have a dynamic array. This is
   allowed in the bindless proposal because the content-timeline doesn't
   know if a bindgroup is an error or not.
 - Add tests for all the synchronous validation, updated validation
   rules and some of the validation generating validations errors.

Bugs found with testing:

 - Inversion of the condition for OOB checks on slots.
 - Missing validation of OOB check for the start of the dynamic array.
 - Missed check for frontend layout validity before trying to get the
   BindGroupLayoutInternal.
 - Missing validation of a destroyed dynamic binding array in
   RemoveBinding.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Update BufferCopy to use strong types
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Update BufferCopy to use strong types

And updated all the code that uses it, which is a lot of code.

Also:
- Removed TypedBufferCopy as we can just use BufferCopy
- Added overload of ComputeRequiredBytesInCopy that accepts strong
  types. This overload can only be used post-validation, when there are
  no more undefined values.
- Reworked ComputeBufferImageCopyRegion overloads so that the one that
  accepts TexelCopyBufferLayout calls the one that accepts BufferCopy.
  The latter overload is more useful, and this avoids needless
  conversions from strong to weak types.
- Reworked various other bits to use strong types.

Bug: 424536624
Change-Id: If38240673ed09b2d2cc7235f07db5499ea5fcecc

commit.subject: [uniformity] fix uniformity when loop bodies have returns
commit.message:
[uniformity] fix uniformity when loop bodies have returns

When a loop body has a return then it can cut off control flow
entirely. Function calls that might have required uniformity
may no longer be reached, and should not cause a uniformity error.

Also, the return may be taken non-uniformly, and hence the other
remaining invocations may complete the loop nonuniformily. In these
cases code after the loop may now be exposed to nonuniform execution,
which should trigger a uniformity error.

This patch overhauls the uniformity analysis for loops.

See https://github.com/gpuweb/gpuweb/issues/5364

Bug: 452692768
Change-Id: I6a6a696457f17dfa3be4e0c2fecd895bd058c254

commit.subject: [uniformity] relax uniformity when loop bodies have returns
commit.message:
[uniformity] relax uniformity when loop bodies have returns

See https://github.com/gpuweb/gpuweb/issues/5364

When a loop body has a return then it can cut off control flow
entirely. Function calls that might have required uniformity
may no longer be reached, and should not cause a uniformity error.

Also, the return may be taken non-uniformly, and hence the other
remaining invocations may complete the loop nonuniformily. In these
cases code after the loop may now be exposed to nonuniform execution,
which should trigger a uniformity error.

The tests add a small domain-specific language to test various
combinations of statement behaviours (break, return, next, continue)
and various placements of uniformity "attackers" and "detectors".

This patch is part 1: loop without continuing.

This includes 4 cases that fail due to the conservatism.

commit.subject: Allow c2y-extensions
commit.message:
Allow c2y-extensions

Passes in -Wno-c2y-extensions when building Dawn in a standalone
checkout. The use of -pedantic causes -Wc2y-extensions to be added
automatically, which is currently flagging use of __COUNTER__ in some
histogram macros when rolling some build-related dependencies to be
consistent with Chromium.

Since these histograms were largely copied from Chromium and Chromium
continues to use __COUNTER__ in their version, allow usage in Dawn.

Bug: 452840620
Change-Id: I97d431a64c3f66afe639b3f5fcfe2a8ad62c9d73

commit.subject: Skip emitting barriers from MapAsync
commit.message:
Skip emitting barriers from MapAsync

Emitting a barrier from BufferVk::MapAsyncImpl() should never be
necessary due to TransitionMappableBuffersEagerly(). If the buffer
hasn't been used on GPU in commands for next submit then an eager
transition already emitted required barrier. If the buffer is used on
GPU for next submit then an eager transition will emit the required
barrier immediately before vkQueueSubmit() which MapAsync() waits on
completion for.

commit.subject: vulkan: Initialize buffer padding on CPU
commit.message:
vulkan: Initialize buffer padding on CPU

There is special code to eagerly transition buffer usage back to
MapWrite from UploadData(). This was a workaround for host visible
buffers that had padding bytes that were initialized on GPU that isn't
desirable. Change the buffer padding zero initialization code to
initialize padding bytes on CPU if buffer is host visible instead.

This also requires changing NonzeroClearResourcesOnCreationForTesting
path for host visible buffers since that must happen before zero
initializing the padding bytes.

Bug: 460180744
Change-Id: I1ada9e30919ee3acb4c3c7ebbbfe13d0c41f005c

commit.message:
vulkan: Initialize buffer padding on CPU

There is special code to eagerly transition buffer usage back to
MapWrite from UploadData(). This is workaround for host visible buffers
so they can use the fast upload path in case padding bytes were

buffer padding zero initialization code to initialize padding bytes on

path for host visible buffers since that must happen before zero
initializing the padding bytes.

UploadData() is also modified to only zero initialize data if memcpy()
isn't going to write to the full buffer. This matches the behavior in
EnsureDataInitializedAsDestination() when buffer is initialized on GPU.

commit.subject: [tint][val] Merge Locations + Blend Src and IOAttributes validation
commit.message:
[tint][val] Merge Locations + Blend Src and IOAttributes validation

This CL moves the iterating over various IO objecs (params, returns,
and MSVs) into ValidateIOAttributes, so there can be a single callsite
in CheckFunction. The original implemetnation is moved off into an
impl function ValidateIOAttributesImpl.

The logic for CheckEntryPointLocationsAndBlendSrc is broken up from 2
passes into 3 passes; populate context, validate blend_src, and
validate location.

These passes are moved into the top-level ValidateIOAttributes
function, so that all of the IO attributes validation is invoked via a
single call.

The logic for validating blend_src and location is NOT moved into
IOAttributeCheckers in this CL, because that will require significant
reworking of the existing logic, and grouping all of the IO attributes
logic into a single callsite is an improvement to the code's
readability, even if the migration to Checker does not happen.

Bug: 455376684

Change-Id: I41fe254419952a5369e6594bdfb3ae8f1d452f7f

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Fix BlitTextureToBuffer handling of undefined bytesPerRow and rowsPerImage
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Fix BlitTextureToBuffer handling of undefined bytesPerRow and rowsPerImage

Make sure to use layout values that are not undefined when calling
BlitTextureToBuffer. This is done via
ApplyDefaultTexelCopyBufferLayoutOptions, which replaces undefined
values with the real values, correctly computed in block space and
aligned. The code in BlitTextureToBuffer was handling these values when
undefined incorreclty. In practice, this means they would do the wrong
thing when bytesPerRow is undefined and the texture is compressed.

Bug: 462167738
Change-Id: I1a78bb5b17ad880b06a6b82d1289781ddaada5b4

commit.message:
[tint][val] Add testing coverage for @color validation

Missed doing this when I migrated the colour validation code.

I have also refactored ValidateIOAttributes to only fire one type of
error per check, i.e. if this is the wrong entry point usage don't
bother with running the check function, since they tended to be a bit
noisy in the logs.

Cleaned up some existing tests that were using wrong entry point type,
since with the above refactoring we wouldn't be getting the later
error messages.

commit.subject: GL: add a toggle to allow GL context to current on different threads
commit.message:
GL: add a toggle to allow GL context to current on different threads

This toggle is intended to be used with ScopedMakeCurrent.
- If this toggle is on, ScopedMakeCurrent will unmake current the
context so that it can be used on another thread.
- If this toggle is off, then ScopedMakeCurrent won't do that. And the
GL context will only be made current on a single thread.

Certain use cases such as WebGPU will only use GL context on a single
thread. Thus disabling this toggle would avoid overheads of frequent
context switches.

Bug: 451928481
Change-Id: I33b85dfdb6180f2d570faa2f5920bb31009ceae6

commit.subject: GL: Add toggle for multi-threaded context current
commit.message:
GL: Add toggle for multi-threaded context current

Adds a toggle to control whether a GL context can be made current on
different threads.

When disabled, the context is assumed to be used on a single thread,
avoiding the overhead of frequent context switches. This is beneficial
for use cases like WebGPU that operate on a single thread.

Bug: 451928481
Change-Id: I33b85dfdb6180f2d570faa2f5920bb31009ceae6

commit.subject: tint/hlsl: Implement ArrayLengthFromImmediates support
commit.message:
tint/hlsl: Implement ArrayLengthFromImmediates support

This change enables HLSL backend to use immediate data blocks (root
constants) for storing buffer size information, eliminating the need
for a separate uniform buffer when computing array lengths.

Why:
- Reduces descriptor table usage in D3D12 by storing buffer sizes in
  root constants instead of requiring a dedicated uniform buffer
- Provides performance benefit by avoiding an extra buffer binding
- Brings HLSL backend to parity with MSL backend which already supports
  this optimization

Components affected:
- ArrayLengthFromUniformOptions: Added buffer_sizes_offset field to
  support immediate block storage at a specified offset
- PopulateBindingRelatedOptions: Fixed to properly copy the new
  buffer_sizes_offset field from input options
- HLSL raise pipeline: Added buffer_sizes array creation in immediate
  data config, packed as array<vec4<u32>> for 16-byte alignment
- Transform selection: Conditionally uses ArrayLengthFromImmediates
  when buffer_sizes_offset is set, otherwise falls back to
  ArrayLengthFromUniform
- Added ArrayLength_RobustnessAndArrayLengthFromImmediates test

Bug: dawn:2428
Change-Id: I42d6dc3e172513d853fe502e60d337c22142be95

commit.message:
[cts] skip const_array_elements:sizeDivisor=1 on Intel Linux

Testing on a Linux Intel Iris Xe Graphics TGL GT2,
I confirmed that if the Mesa cache is empty, the test
fails with a timeout.  If the Mesa cache is warm from
a prior run, then the test passes quickly.

commit.subject: [tint][val] Improve input_index_attachement validation
commit.message:
[tint][val] Improve input_index_attachement validation

This is less of a migration, and instead using the ValidateIOAttribute
framework to test for the attribute being on function params and
returns, which are not Vars. The original Var code is retained to
cover MSVs and other cases like function scoped vars.

This involved loosen when ValidatorIOAttributes runs to handle MSVs
that are not in the In or Out address space. This will also be needed
for dealing with binding_point in the future, which is why I went with
a more systematic change instead of just special casing it.

Bug: 455376684
Change-Id: Ie7fa4cc17d91db3afc6c0a083d0643d603c3b5c9

commit.subject: m143: D3D11: Cache shader objects from same shader blobs.
commit.message:
m143: D3D11: Cache shader objects from same shader blobs.

Currently, Dawn only caches the shader *blob* (the compiled HLSL
bytecode) but not the actual D3D11 shader *objects*
(ID3D11VertexShader, ID3D11PixelShader, ID3D11ComputeShader). The
creation of these shader objects from the blob can be a non-trivial
operation, impacting performance.

This change introduces caching for the D3D11 shader objects themselves.
The caching mechanism uses the SHA3 hash of the shader blob as the key
to store and retrieve the D3D11 shader objects. This allows for reuse
when multiple pipelines use the same underlying shader blob, thereby
reducing redundant object creation and improving performance.

with the loosen capability (i.e. during Shader I/O), instead of

correctly setting their capabilities.

in the interface.

commit.subject: [tint][val] Proof-of-concept for reworking IOAttribute validation
commit.message:
[tint][val] Proof-of-concept for reworking IOAttribute validation

Use a more data/table driven pattern for IOAttribute validation, akin
to BuiltInValidation.

Invariant validation is reimplemented using this new framework as a
proof-of-concept, other IOAttributes will be migrated in follow on
CLs.

An enum and ToString for tagging IOAttributes is added to allow baking
into the checker what attribute is being validated.

There is also some minor clean-ups to related code
included. Specifically for the called impl in WalkTypeAndMembers the
context param is moved to the beginning of the param list to match the
form as other calls, and CheckVertexEntryPoint is renamed to
CheckPositionPresentForVertexOutput, since that is all it does now.

Issue: 455376684

Change-Id: I791210b7d1d12ff99879fff55223592803e0504a

commit.message:
[WebGPU backend] Make sure RenderBundle is created once and reuse at ExecuteBundles

Make native::RenderBundleEncoder and native::RenderBundle extensiable
and make webgpu::RenderBundleEncoder and webgpu::RenderBundle.

Call GetOrEncodeInnerRenderBundle explicitly at
ExecuteBundle to make sure things like DrawIndirectCmd.indirectBuffer
are properly initialized.

Bug: 413053623
Change-Id: I19be8d2ef137637b2af72c96314466680fa212c8

commit.subject: Handle `Element` override in subgroup matrix
commit.message:
Handle `Element` override in subgroup matrix

The subgroup matrix type reports a splat count of `columns` but
currently does not override the `Element` method, so all the subtypes
end up being `nullptr`. Add an override to return the actual subtype.

Fixed: 460323251
Change-Id: I48948a22c3f3dc739d039c1ecc2a99d3724a6d7e

the error up.

commit.subject: d3d11: Don't hold D3D11 scope lock when waiting for queue serial
commit.message:
d3d11: Don't hold D3D11 scope lock when waiting for queue serial

Avoids holding the D3D11 scope lock in WaitForQueueSerialImpl
to prevent potential deadlocks with drivers that may acquire the
same lock.

The scope lock is a performance optimization that prevents other
threads from modifying D3D11 states concurrently. However,
WaitForQueueSerialImpl only polls for completion and doesn't
change any state, so the lock is not needed.

With multithread protection enabled, individual D3D11 calls are already
thread-safe.

Bug: 434070352
Change-Id: Id4dab2774cc44bc93b9ba00cb68ed66b20297bcc

Refactor: Add KDoc links and improve reference validation in generator

Major changes:
- Adds External Links: Converts internal `@ref` tags for non-API
    concepts (e.g., `ErrorScopes`, `CallbackStatuses`) and points to github documentation.
- Improves Validation: Refactors `webgpu_json_utility.py` to use
    new helper functions for more accurate reference validation, handling
    method names, hyphenated names, and `wgpu`-prefixes.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Sepatate deferErrors to a boolean in EncodingContext
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Sepatate deferErrors to a boolean in EncodingContext

The logic in EncodingContext::HandleError decides whether the error
should be deferred until Finish() or if it should be immediately
forwarded to the device. Future CLs will change that logic so to make
them more clear, separate the condition as a boolean in advance.

This is in preparation for changes error handling of encoders to match
the latest specification.

Bug: 449980070
Change-Id: I0d4b44a4f662b1e5246d496fa362e27c7b34ad77

commit.subject: [vulkan] Denylist SubgroupMatrix for Mesa older than 25.2
commit.message:
[vulkan] Denylist SubgroupMatrix for Mesa older than 25.2

Older drivers have bugs with subgroup matrix initialization that make
than unsuitable for use with this feature.

This also lets us remove a workaround for OpConstantNull for those
older drivers, which in turn fixes a fuzzer issue.

Fixed: 458689917, 457877789
Change-Id: I6a99a9e509a2dcb11c8a6c9eb377085344b51378

commit.subject: dawn and tint: add a language feature 'immediate_address_space'
commit.message:
dawn and tint: add a language feature 'immediate_address_space'

- Added 'immediate_address_space' language feature.
- Effectively deprecates 'chromium_experimental_immediate' langauge
  extension. This is being left in Tint for now because Skia emits this,
  but Tint ignores it for now. Will remove it from Skia after this rolls
  into Chromium. See crbug.com/460481195.
- Removed 'enable_immediate_data' toggle that I added recently. Instead,
  we test if the new language feature is enabled.
- ValidationTest changes:
  - Added ValidationTestWithParam
  - Added GetWGSLBlocklistedFeatures() vfunc to allow tests to add
    values to the blocklist
- Made ImmediateDataDisableTest parameterized so that we can test that
  the feature is properly disabled by either blocklisting or when
  AllowUnsafeAPIs is disabled.
- Tint resolver looks for language feature rather than extension. Fixed
  up unit tests and e2e tests.

commit.subject: Optimize Dawn Wire WriteTexture
commit.message:
Optimize Dawn Wire WriteTexture

Reduces the number of memcpys that are done when uploading texture data
via WriteTexture using the wire client. Does so by directly managing the
allocation of shared memory and writing to that rather than copying the
data to the wire command buffer first, which may involve chunking and
additional copies.

In tests so far this performs up to 2X better than the previous
WriteTexture implementation, depending on data size. (Larger uploads
typically see a bigger improvement.)

Very similar to recent WriteBuffer optimizations proposed by Loko:
https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/271535

Bug: 441900745
Change-Id: Ie85e2d38e4db9ad85465640a4f0d65f07c69fa78

commit.subject: [tint] Polyfill 'position' for vulkan in muliti-sampling
commit.message:
[tint] Polyfill 'position' for vulkan in muliti-sampling

The WebGPU/WGSL SPEC specifies that 'position' be pixel centered.
For msl/HLSL this will always be the case even with multi-sampled
fragments. However vulkan does not appear to always behave this way [0].
This change polyfills 'position' in the case where we require
known consistent behavior.

This change allocates an additional variable (vec4f) for the
interpolant that was introduced to emulate the 'position' builtin.



[0]
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bEvj-7nSeynmywCUnSetpp06jcIeUjmmFBeOo8-pJLg/edit?pli=1&tab=t.0

commit.subject: [tint] Polyfill 'position' for vulkan in muliti-sampling
commit.message:
[tint] Polyfill 'position' for vulkan in muliti-sampling

The WebGPU/WGSL SPEC specifies that 'position' be pixel centered.
For MSL/HLSL this will always be the case even with multi-sampled
fragments. However vulkan does not appear to always behave this way [0].
This change polyfills 'position' in the case where we require
known consistent behavior.

This change allocates an additional variable (vec4f) for the
interpolant that is introduced to emulate the 'position' builtin.

For a few select devices (intel) this means we need to drop the limit
maxInterStageShaderVariables from 28 to 16.

commit.subject: [ir][val] Implement better type/struct traversal
commit.message:
[ir][val] Implement better type/struct traversal

Adds in a new function WalkTypeAndMembers for walking down the type hierarchy
into struct members and running an impl function on each step.

This replaces a variety of existing implementations/patterns in the IR
validator, standardizing onto one implementation and setting the groundwork for
future refactoring that will unify all of the IO attribute validation logic into
a more data driven pattern.

There is some cleanups to the existing code, like re-targeting errors messages
to the declaration of MSVs instead of the entry point that references them.

Some places of multiple walks have been merged where it was trivial to do,
though some of the more complex cases have not been merged. Future CLs will do
more invasive refactoring that will clean up these instances.

Bug: 455376684

Change-Id: If7ba17e6f8465bf78f172187140f44a9cfd95dab

commit.subject: [spirv] Make all access chain indices unsigned.
commit.message:
[spirv] Make all access chain indices unsigned.

For any `OpAccessChain` in SPIR-V it is a validation error to have a
negative constant index value. In order to make sure we never emit
negative indices, always bitcast the index to an unsigned value before
passing to the access chain.

There are currently only two ways this can happen, by disabling
robustness or but the disabling of runtime array robustness. In the case
of the former, robustness has been disabled, so it's on the caller to
make sure the index was never negative. In the case of the latter we
only do this when we have RobustBufferAccess2 enabled and it will
handling the clamping for us.

Fixed: 459509275
Change-Id: I784cb3c8dbc3e3c907402094940fabed16138827

so this CL adds a step to filter them out the unavailable configs when
they are queried instead.

commit.subject: GL: Skip redundant calls to eglMakeCurrent().
commit.message:
GL: Skip redundant calls to eglMakeCurrent().

The EGL spec requires that eglMakeCurrent() cause a flush, even when the
call is a no-op. By avoiding redundant calls, we avoid the flush.

This is good for a 17X speedup on desk_chalkboard:

Graphite/Dawn/GLES, before:
curr/maxrss	loops	min	median	mean	max	stddev		config	bench
 195/199 MB	1	147ms	164ms	165ms	200ms	6%		grdawn_gles	desk_chalkboard.skp_1

Graphite/Dawn/GLES, after:
curr/maxrss	loops	min	median	mean	max	stddev		config	bench
 204/205 MB	1	8.73ms	9.59ms	9.66ms	12.3ms	4%		grdawn_gles	desk_chalkboard.skp_1

Ganesh/GLES:
curr/maxrss	loops	min	median	mean	max	stddev		config	bench
  86/139 MB	1	9.39ms	11.2ms	11.2ms	15.2ms	8%		gles	desk_chalkboard.skp_1

Change-Id: I12cab41f028be4b94e36d951c0fbce4f6dfe5eca

commit.message:
[dawn][node] Add support for immediates.

This adds (untested for now) support for immediates in dawn.node. The
logic from writeBuffer to convert (dat, offset, size) to a C pointer and
size is extracted to its own function and reused in setImmediates.

commit.subject: Revert "D3D11: Create shader objects asynchronously."
commit.message:
Revert "D3D11: Create shader objects asynchronously."

This reverts commit ba3c279d624f208de212db3f8e482fb6a01159de.

Reason for revert: Seems to cause the hangs in crbug.com/459978952

Original change's description:
> D3D11: Create shader objects asynchronously.
>
> This change makes the creation of D3D11 shader objects
> (ID3D11VertexShader, etc.) asynchronous. Currently, these objects must
> be ready when a pipeline is used for command buffer encoding. However,
> they are only strictly needed when the command buffer is submitted.
>
> By deferring the creation until submission, this change avoids blocking
> the encoding thread if the shader takes a long time to be created. This
> allows for more ample time for shader creation to happen in parallel
> with command recording.
>
> Bug: 439845637, chromium:40266176
> Change-Id: Ib5c678bdcf5218d941214db46aa6b5b236bace46

commit.subject: D3D11: Create shader objects asynchronously.
commit.message:
D3D11: Create shader objects asynchronously.

This change makes the creation of D3D11 shader objects
(ID3D11VertexShader, etc.) asynchronous. The actual D3D11 shader
objects are only required when the command buffer referencing them is
submitted to the GPU.

By creating them asynchronously, we can avoid blocking pipeline
creation on the main thread, allowing the CPU to continue processing
other work in parallel. The pipeline will wait for the future to be
ready only when the shader object is needed for command submission.

Bug: 439845637, chromium:40266176
Change-Id: Ib5c678bdcf5218d941214db46aa6b5b236bace46

This change makes the creation of D3D11 shader objects
(ID3D11VertexShader, etc.) asynchronous. The shader objects are not
required when recording the command buffer; they are only needed when
the command buffer referencing them is submitted to the GPU.

By creating them asynchronously, pipeline creation no longer blocks
the calling thread. This allows the CPU to continue processing other
work in parallel, since shader objects are only needed at command
submission, not during recording.

commit.subject: D3D11: Create shader objects asynchronously.
commit.message:
D3D11: Create shader objects asynchronously.

This change makes the creation of D3D11 shader objects
(ID3D11VertexShader, etc.) asynchronous. Currently, these objects must
be ready when a pipeline is used for command buffer encoding. However,
they are only strictly needed when the command buffer is submitted.

By deferring the creation until submission, this change avoids blocking
the encoding thread if the shader takes a long time to be created. This
allows for more ample time for shader creation to happen in parallel
with command recording.

Bug: 439845637, chromium:40266176
Change-Id: Ib5c678bdcf5218d941214db46aa6b5b236bace46

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Finalize deprecation of lax inherited view usage
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Finalize deprecation of lax inherited view usage

When we added GPUTextureUsage.usage there was a sublte breaking change
that we added a deprecation for: creating an SRGB view from a storage
RGBA/BGRA8Unorm texture is now supposed to fail.

 - Finalize the deprecation by adding the validation, updating tests and
   removing the deprecation warning.
 - Rework validation of TextureUsage to separate the `usage != 0` check.
   This is necessary because with the "internalUsage" extension it is
   possible to create a texture view with "usage = 0" (when the parent
   texture only has internal usages and no external usages).
 - Add a test for that corner case, as it is triggered in Chromium in
   some SharedImage paths.

Bug: 363903526
Change-Id: Ib899426621c717224d3478716060f422cb9e1bc9

commit.subject: [spirv] Polyfill 8-bit subgroup matrix construct
commit.message:
[spirv] Polyfill 8-bit subgroup matrix construct

SPIR-V requires that the value passed to OpCompositeConstruct has the
same type as the matrix, so we need to convert it to an 8-bit
value. This was already done for construct instructions generated by
the matrix-scalar builtin polyfills.

Update the validator to allow either the 8-bit or 32-bit types for an
8-bit subgroup matrix constructor, to satisfy both WGSL and SPIR-V.

Fixed: 459800105
Change-Id: I46626a3c465bd8394458878862d0ebd3961a52a8

commit.subject: Optimize Dawn Wire WriteBuffer
commit.message:
Optimize Dawn Wire WriteBuffer

Reduces the number of memcpys that are done when uploading buffer data
via WriteBuffer using the wire client. Does so by directly managing the
allocation of shared memory and writing to that rather than copying the
data to the wire command buffer first, which may involve chunking and
additional copies.

In tests so far this performs up to 2X better than the previous
WriteBuffer implementation, depending on data size. (Larger uploads
typically see a bigger improvement.)

Derived from Loko's prototype:
https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/269134
https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/269814

Alternative to my previous effort to move the WriteBuffer implementation
client-side: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/270895

Bug: 441900745
Change-Id: I1d7aa1b7f64e2ac6582512d64a4b981f2e208cd6

commit.subject: [dawn][wire] Always transfer null string view using UINT64_MAX
commit.message:
[dawn][wire] Always transfer null string view using UINT64_MAX

In WebView, the renderer can be 32-bit while the GPU process is 64-bit
(see https://crbug.com/374281034#comment2). I don't think we have ever
tested this before - it's now running on blink_perf.webgpu - but
apparently somehow the only thing that's broken is StringView
serialization, in which the client will use WGPU_STRLEN=UINT32_MAX and
the server will use WGPU_STRLEN=UINT64_MAX.

Fixed: 457989891
Change-Id: Idc85789e38c0d9d235aaa37b015b4e9b1eecd482

commit.subject: Kotlin: Reland: Async adapter returns only the actual return value.
commit.message:
Kotlin: Reland: Async adapter returns only the actual return value.

A 'Return' wrapper class is no longer created or used.

The 'status' and 'message' values are used to raise exceptions when relevant,
but not passed to the client.

Relanded following removal of circular dependency between bindings
and the helper clases when exceptions were in the helpers.

Additional reland fix following improved understanding of Dawn errors and
API council requirements:

- Where the actual payload is ErrorType a custom exception is created. This
allows popErrorScope() to raise the popped exception (Java-idiomatic).

Bug: 456671498
Change-Id: If652cc95b80f29044f5883f98b35470f7bf4984a

commit.subject: [tint][val] Rework how `@builtin(...)` is validated
commit.message:
[tint][val] Rework how `@builtin(...)` is validated

Refactors the existing checker implementation to support the special
cased built-ins like @builtin(position), so that their special
handling can be removed. This refactoring changes the error logging to
be explict about what the builtin was attached to, e.g. a vertex
shader input, and provides what the valid options are.

This CL also changes the capability to allow clip_distance on scalars
to also allow vectors, since that is needed by the HLSL
backend. Trying to split them into two capabilities leads to a bunch
of duplicated instances of them and more complex logic in the
validator. (The original validation logic had an oversight that
allowed this construct to pass unintentionally)

Issue: 455376684
Change-Id: Ia5dac3782158c2e1acc3d0505fa7fdf4a1057f3b

commit.subject: [tint][val] Rework how `@builtin(...)` is validated
commit.message:
[tint][val] Rework how `@builtin(...)` is validated

Refactors the existing checker implementation to support the special
cased built-ins like @builtin(position), so that their special
handling can be removed. This refactoring changes the error logging to
be explicit about what the builtin was attached to, e.g. a vertex
shader input, and provides what the valid options are.

This CL also changes the capability to allow clip_distance on scalars
to also allow vectors, since that is needed by the HLSL
backend. Trying to split them into two capabilities leads to a bunch
of duplicated instances of them and more complex logic in the
validator. (The original validation logic had an oversight that
allowed this construct to pass unintentionally)

Issue: 455376684

commit.subject: [gn] Remove custom GN rules for abseil-cpp
commit.message:
[gn] Remove custom GN rules for abseil-cpp

Previously due to how Skia used Dawn, we had to maintain a seperate
custom set of build rules for abseil-cpp. Since Skia has moved to
using the CMake build for Dawn, we can now remove these rules.

When moving to use the true abseil-cpp GN rules, I have migrated our
targets to depend on the top-level target, instead of manually
converting all of the targets we directly us, since at this point due
to transitive dependencies we are including most of abseil-cpp anyway.

I retained the custom config to suppress some warnings coming from
abseil-cpp, since otherwise I was getting build failures due to
'-Werror' and the abseil-cpp headers being included. This could be
worked around in other ways like supressing these warnings at the
inclusion site, turning off the related warnings for the entire build
or treating abseil-cpp as a system library/header but I decided to
just retain our existing fix.

Issue: 456225724
Change-Id: I807edda6a1bdd41ba4eaad8e1bd3601f7e15be1d

commit.subject: [gn] Remove custom GN rules for abseil-cpp
commit.message:
[gn] Remove custom GN rules for abseil-cpp

Previously due to how Skia used Dawn, we had to maintain a separate
custom set of build rules for abseil-cpp. Since Skia has moved to
using the CMake build for Dawn, we can now remove these rules.

When moving to use the true abseil-cpp GN rules, I have migrated our
targets to depend on the top-level target, instead of manually
converting all of the targets we directly use, since at this point due
to transitive dependencies we are including most of abseil-cpp anyway.

I retained the custom config to suppress some warnings coming from
abseil-cpp, since otherwise I was getting build failures due to
'-Werror' and the abseil-cpp headers being included. This could be
worked around in other ways like suppressing these warnings at the
inclusion site, turning off the related warnings for the entire build
or if GN supported system libraries/headers, but I decided to just
retain our existing fix.

This requires rolling the abseil-cpp and adding //tools/win in DEPS

commit.subject: [gn] Remove custom GN rules for abseil-cpp
commit.message:
[gn] Remove custom GN rules for abseil-cpp

Previously due to how Skia used Dawn, we had to maintain a separate
custom set of build rules for abseil-cpp. Since Skia has moved to
using the CMake build for Dawn, we can now remove these rules.

When moving to use the true abseil-cpp GN rules, I have migrated our
targets to depend on the top-level target, instead of manually
converting all of the targets we directly use, since at this point due
to transitive dependencies we are including most of abseil-cpp anyway.

I retained the custom config to suppress some warnings coming from
abseil-cpp, since otherwise I was getting build failures due to
'-Werror' and the abseil-cpp headers being included. This could be
worked around in other ways like suppressing these warnings at the
inclusion site, turning off the related warnings for the entire build
or if GN supported system libraries/headers, but I decided to just
retain our existing fix.

This requires rolling abseil-cpp and adding //tools/win in DEPS.
I have also adjusted various DEPS hashes related to the toolchain to
match those used by ANGLE. Since Windows was producing missing symbol
errors, so they likely had gotten out of sync, and ANGLE's builds are
working with abseil-cpp.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Make immediates 64 bytes by default on core backends
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Make immediates 64 bytes by default on core backends

Set maxImmediateSize to 64 for tier0. We no longer have multiple tiers,
so apart from compat, all backends now support exactly 64 bytes for
immediate data.

- Got rid of  kDefaultMaxImmediateDataBytes since we no longer have
  multiple tiers. Also renamed kMaxSupportedImmediateDataBytes to
  kMaxImmediateDataBytes for the same reason.

- Added EnableImmediateData toggle to control this feature. We were
  previously using AllowUnsafeAPIs to enable this feature. For
  convenience, we if AllowUnsafeAPIs is enabled, we enable
  EnableImmediateData.

- We now validate that the EnableImmediateData toggle is on rather than
  check that decriptor->immediateSize > maxImmediateSize or that
  maxImmediateSize is non-zero. This simplifies the validation logic.

- Removed DeviceCreationTest.AdapterMaxImmediateSize test since it
  expects that immediates are only enabled iff the adapter has
  AllowUnsafeAPIs, but now actually depends on the EnableImmediateData
  toggle.

- Reworked RequestDeviceWithImmediateDataValidationTest.HigherIsBetter
  test to validate that we always get the same value for the
  maxImmediateSize now that we no longer have tiers.

Change-Id: I97bbef016c4d57d9ae1b545c73afa9984c350db1

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Make immediates 64 bytes by default on core backends
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Make immediates 64 bytes by default on core backends

Set maxImmediateSize to 64 for tier0. We no longer have multiple tiers,
so apart from compat, all backends now support exactly 64 bytes for
immediate data.

- Got rid of kDefaultMaxImmediateDataBytes since we no longer have
  multiple tiers. Also renamed kMaxSupportedImmediateDataBytes to
  kMaxImmediateDataBytes for the same reason.

- Added EnableImmediateData toggle to control this feature. We were
  previously using AllowUnsafeAPIs to enable this feature. For
  convenience, if AllowUnsafeAPIs is enabled, we enable
  EnableImmediateData.

- We now validate that the EnableImmediateData toggle is on rather than
  check that decriptor->immediateSize > maxImmediateSize or that
  maxImmediateSize is non-zero. This simplifies the validation logic.

- Removed DeviceCreationTest.AdapterMaxImmediateSize test since it
  expects that immediates are only enabled iff the adapter has
  AllowUnsafeAPIs, but now actually depends on the EnableImmediateData
  toggle.

- Reworked RequestDeviceWithImmediateDataValidationTest.HigherIsBetter
  test to validate that we always get the same value for the
  maxImmediateSize now that we no longer have tiers.

Bug: 458081201

commit.subject: Refactor buffer barrier tracking
commit.message:
Refactor buffer barrier tracking

Decouple the tracking from CommandRecordingContext. The tracking isn't
thread safe and the only part that needs CommandRecordingContext is
emitting barriers.

Have TrackUsageAndGetResourceBarrier() return BufferBarrier instead of
barrier in CommandRecordingContext. The barrier was immediately
emitted from TransitionUsageNow() so continue to do that. In
TransitionMappableBuffersEagerly() and PrepareResourcesForSyncScope() on
the other hand barriers from multiple buffers were merged.
PrepareResourcesForSyncScope() also tracks vertex vs non-vertex barriers
separately and that should continue to work.

commit.subject: Refactor buffer barrier tracking
commit.message:
Refactor buffer barrier tracking

Decouple the tracking from CommandRecordingContext. The tracking isn't
thread safe and the only part that needs CommandRecordingContext is
emitting barriers.

The important change here is TrackUsageAndGetResourceBarrier() returns a
BufferBarrier instead of storing it in CommandRecordingContext. That
barrier is either immediately emitted or barriers for multiple buffers
are merged by the caller then emitted. PrepareResourcesForSyncScope()
still tracks separate vertex vs non-vertex barriers.

This also makes it easy to skip emitting barriers from MapAsyncImpl() as
a follow up.

commit.message:
vulkan: Don't add barrier for map->map

BufferVk had a condition to avoid adding a barrier for map usage
followed by map write usage. The same logic was missing from map read
branch so add it. We don't need barriers for map followed by map.

Bug: 425472913
Change-Id: I9293fe90306a43cdca78c0b7a468ebd184813a44

commit.subject: Kotlin: Replace status returns with exceptions
commit.message:
Kotlin: Replace status returns with exceptions

Modify the templates to convert WebGPU methods returning only status
codes into Kotlin functions returning `Unit` that throw `DawnException`
on failure. This aligns with idiomatic Kotlin and replaces generic
`java.lang.Error` usage in JNI.

Change-Id: Ief6ee10cb39726d629b10ad718de0cf9516cd063

commit.subject: Fix mMapData race
commit.message:
Fix mMapData race

BufferBase::mMapData is accessed from UnmapInternal() when PendingMap
and it's assumed that it contains Ref<MapAsyncEvent>. The variable is
also written from BufferBase::FinalizeMap(). There is no mutex that
protects against reading in UnmapInternal() while writing in
FinalizeMap() which is problematic.

Fix this by protecting both locations by the same mutex. The existing
mutex in MapAsyncEvent isn't usable since we have to access the variable
and dereference it to get mutex from BufferBase. Add a global mutex
shared between all buffers that is tightly scoped to just resetting
pointer variables.

Split mMapdata into mMappedPointer and mPendingMapEvent to make
things easier to understand. Also create a new MapAsyncErrorEvent type
to handle errors that happen before PendingMap to further simplify
things.

Bug: 425472913
Change-Id: Iff75404097037eb23cbdfc633ef48a2dfbd165ed

commit.subject: Fix BufferBase::mMapData race
commit.message:
Fix BufferBase::mMapData race

BufferBase::mMapData is accessed from UnmapInternal() when PendingMap
and it's assumed that it contains Ref<MapAsyncEvent>. The variable is
also written from BufferBase::FinalizeMap(). There is no mutex that
protects against reading in UnmapInternal() while writing in
FinalizeMap() which is problematic.

Fix this by protecting both places Ref<MapAsyncEvent> is reset with the
same mutex. The existing mutex in MapAsyncEvent isn't usable since we
have to access the variable and dereference it to get mutex from
BufferBase. Fix this by making BufferBase support WeakRef and own the
mutex. MapAsyncEvent can promote a WeakRef<BufferBase>, if promotion
fails the buffer has been destroyed and there is no possible race. If
promotion is successful then MapAsyncEvent is able to lock mutex before
proceeding.

Additionally MapAsyncEvent::mStatus is also initially accessed with the
same mutex locked. The status is changed to not be success if outcomes
race and Unmap() path wins, so if MapAsyncEvent::Complete() sees a
non-success status it knows map was aborted and doesn't need to bother
checking mPendingMapEvent.

mMapdata is split into mMappedPointer and mPendingMapEvent to make code
easier to understand.

Bug: 425472913
Change-Id: Iff75404097037eb23cbdfc633ef48a2dfbd165ed

commit.subject: Plumb Angle virtualization group
commit.message:
Plumb Angle virtualization group

When we use Angle/GL as a backend for dawn, caller need to be able to
specify angle virtualization group number to avoid any conflicts with
the GL context the caller uses for themselves, because:
* it's undefined behavior to use different contexts from the same group
  on the different threads.
* Context must use the same group for texture sharing to work for
  desktop GL.

Bug: chromium:423632846
Change-Id: Ifa7b02bc8dd929c445a89f0a350a2acef50fbd7b

commit.subject: [gn] Remove support for building without //build
commit.message:
[gn] Remove support for building without //build

This was required as part of supporting Skia building Dawn via gn, due
to the lack of access shared chromium tools in their build
environment. Since Skia is now using the CMake builds, this support is
no longer needed.

Specifically this remove the build variables `dawn_had_build` and
`tint_has_build` along with their related guards, etc.

Fixes: 456225724
Change-Id: I597a93b1f578cc67f186a6097f2171335def21da

commit.subject: [msl] Fixup subgroup matrix initialization.
commit.message:
[msl] Fixup subgroup matrix initialization.

When creating a `subgroup_matrix` in WGSL when provided with an argument
will create a filled matrix. The MSL behaviour when calling the type
constructor is to make a diagonal matrix. Switch to using
`make_filled_simdgroup_matrix` instead to match the expected WGSL
behaviour.

An empty construct call is converted to a make filled simdgroup matrix
with the appropriate 0 value to make sure the memory is initialized.

Fixed: 457816671
Change-Id: I48ffd3a5ca6b5f0d88d8900d469e8814af1170ef

commit.subject: Avoid holding the device lock in CreatePipelineAsyncEvent callbacks.
commit.message:
Avoid holding the device lock in CreatePipelineAsyncEvent callbacks.

Gather the arguments needed for mCallback and then release the device
lock before calling it. If mCallback is reentrant and releases the
device, DeviceBase::FlushCallbackTaskQueue assumes that the lock is not
held.

Bug: 448426209, 448892602, 442827275
Change-Id: I378d6f44800d426c05974369f584a9aaccc6b00b

commit.subject: d3d12: optimize root signature slot usage for dynamic storage buffers
commit.message:
d3d12: optimize root signature slot usage for dynamic storage buffers

Rather than bind dynamic storage buffers to root descriptors as [base
offset + dynamic offset, size], bind them instead to the root descriptor
table at [base offset, full size - base offset], and store the dynamic
offset as a root constant. The dynamic offsets are fed to Tint via
ArrayOffsetFromUniform, and thus are applied at shader runtime by
reading the offsets from a UBO and adding them to all reads/writes of
dynamic storage buffers.

Before this change, each dynamic storage buffer binding would use 3 root
signature slots: 2 for the root descriptor binding, and 1 for the buffer
length. With this change, each binding now takes 2 root signature slots:
1 for the buffer length (as before), and 1 for the buffer offset. This
frees up 8 slots (maxDynamicStorageBuffersPerPipelineLayout) in total.

Also, because dynamic storage buffers bindings are now in the root
descriptor table, we disable robustness checks on them, just like we do
for non-dynamic storage buffers, since descriptor table accesses are
well defined.

Other things to point out:

- Added BindGroupTests.DynamicOffsetsWithAtomicOperations test to cover
  the case of atomic operations on dynamic buffers. This is because
  along with (RW)ByteAddressBuffer Load and Store functions, the
  Interlocked* functions are the ones that take an offset, so we want to
  make sure the dynamic offsets are properly applied.
- Added some useful comments to DynamicBufferOffsetTests.
- Added dawn::ityp::stack_vec::empty()
- Added dawn::ityp::vector::resize(Index, const Value&) overload

Bug: 449703736
